title: The second rooms
hook: struggle and backsliding; Teresa says keep going, don't turn back

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Interior Castle: God at the center, and the door is prayer. Today, the rooms just past the entrance, where it gets harder.

You start something good. A run every morning, a journal, a prayer before bed. The first week is great. The second week, the alarm goes off, it's cold, and a very reasonable voice in your head says: skip it, you're not really the type anyway. You skip three days, and the voice says: see? You've already failed. Might as well stop. Teresa of Ávila knew that voice well. She gives it its own set of rooms in her castle, and she has one piece of advice for anyone standing in them.
screen: `A GOOD START.` → `THE SECOND WEEK.` → `SEE? YOU ALREADY FAILED.`

segments.voice: First, who's here. The second rooms, Teresa says, belong to people who have begun to pray. They've stepped inside, and now they hear God calling them, through a good friend, a sermon, a book, even an illness or a hard season. That's the good news. The hard news: the pull of the old life hasn't gone anywhere. So these rooms, she says, can feel worse than the first ones. You hear the call, and you can't answer it well yet. Second, the voices. Teresa pictures the enemy of the soul whispering reasonable things: your friends will miss you, your health will suffer, other people seem fine without all this. The attacks are gentle, not dramatic. That's what makes them work. Third, falling. Teresa expects people here to fall, and doesn't pretend otherwise. Her advice: don't be discouraged, and don't stop praying. God can bring good even out of the fall. The real danger isn't slipping. It's deciding, after you slip, that you'll never go back in. Fourth, Teresa herself. In her autobiography she admits that as a young nun she gave up prayer for a long time, about a year, maybe more. She felt too unworthy to pray, and she thought that was humility. Later she called it one of the worst mistakes of her life. When she came back, she says, God was waiting. So when Teresa says keep going, she isn't lecturing from the top of a mountain. She's speaking from the second rooms, where she once turned around.
screen: `THE CALL YOU CAN'T YET ANSWER.` · `REASONABLE VOICES SAY GO BACK.` · `YOU WILL FALL. DON'T STOP.` · `TERESA ONCE STOPPED PRAYING.` · then, large: `JUST KEEP GOING.`

segments.voice: Think of something good you started and dropped: a habit of prayer, a walk, a call you used to make. Don't argue about why you stopped; just notice the gap. If you pray, come back the plainest way and tell God you're back, without a speech; if you don't, let these two minutes be your first step back into whatever you dropped.
Falling. What Teresa expects of anyone in the second rooms of her castle: slipping after hearing God's call, but never deciding to stay away. Today's word.
Your line: just keep going. A fall is not the end of the road. Two hundred forty-seven days in.

howItsDone: Catholic spiritual directors often point people who have stopped praying to Teresa's second dwelling places and to her own story, encouraging a simple return to daily prayer without dwelling on guilt.
